engagement_background.objective: SaVida Health engaged Treya Partners to generate $240K–$470K in cost savings through a strategic sourcing program that leverages the company’s enterprise-wide purchasing power, secures best-in-class supplier agreements, and preserves or improves service levels and product quality within a six-month project window ending March 2025.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project covers ten indirect spend categories with a combined baseline spend of approximately $5.3 million (e.g., EMR, Employee Benefits, Lab & Medical Supplies, Small Parcel, IT Hardware, Telecom, Office Supplies, Commercial Print, Waste Management). About 70–90 % of each category’s spend is considered addressable; low-spend/low-opportunity categories may be dropped or re-categorized as the project progresses.
constraints_challenges: Supplier non-responsiveness to data requests, requiring mitigation strategies and unified communications
Potential incumbent supplier pushback and sensitivities during competitive bidding or negotiations
Risk of unsanctioned "side conversations" with suppliers that could undermine a united negotiation front
Limited availability of internal stakeholder time for data provision, interviews, and deliverable review
Need to deliver "quick-hit" savings before year-end 2024, compressing the timeline for early workstreams
Gaps in internal line-item usage data; success depends on obtaining data directly from high-spend suppliers

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic AP/purchasing data exists, but detailed line-item usage and contract information often must be requested from suppliers; no centralized contract repository is indicated.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Historical usage data is incomplete and supplier-specific; both parties agreed that collecting full line-item history for every vendor is impractical and that data gaps will be accepted after reasonable efforts.
